name: Kinoplasmic Resonance Emitter KRE-1 'Halo'
description:
The KRE-1 generates a toroidal field of kinoplasmic resonance — a phenomenon in which a sustained electromagnetic standing wave is shaped into a stable ring geometry by a superconducting coil array within the weapon's emitter head. This ring, roughly 90cm in diameter at standard calibration, propagates forward from the muzzle at approximately 180 meters per second and maintains its toroidal form for up to 22 meters before dissipating. Any matter intersecting the ring's plane during propagation is subjected to a violent shearing force as the standing wave collapses against it, transferring its entire energy load into the intersection point as a circular laceration.

The Halo's visual signature is unmistakable: the toroidal field is faintly luminescent in the violet-ultraviolet range, producing a glowing ring that hangs in the air for a fraction of a second before impact. This visibility is both a tactical liability and the source of the weapon's cultural identity — in GLMZ's underground combat aesthetics, being killed by a Halo is considered a particularly dramatic exit. The ring's geometry means it can theoretically pass through cover — a Halo fired through a window opening will maintain coherence and deliver its energy to whatever occupies the ring's plane on the other side, provided the opening is larger than the ring diameter.

Tessera Corponation designed the KRE-1 for breach and clear operations, where the ability to deliver a cutting force through a doorway or window without exposing the operator to return fire has obvious value. The weapon is heavy and requires a two-second charge cycle between discharges, limiting its rate of fire significantly, but each shot's damage potential is severe — the circular shearing pattern severs limbs and penetrates vehicle windows with equal effectiveness.
specifications: ring diameter: 90cm standard; 60–120cm adjustable propagation velocity: 180 m/s maximum range: 22m before dissipation luminescence: Violet-UV, 380–420nm charge cycle: 2.1 seconds between shots power cell: Tessera TC-20 superconducting cell, 12 discharges weight: 8.4kg dimensions: 78cm length, 31cm width at emitter head cover penetration: Passes through openings larger than ring diameter intact
tactical_use: KRE-1 operators work in two-person teams: one operator handles the heavy weapon while a partner manages target acquisition and cover. The standard tactic is indirect fire — the operator positions outside a structure and fires through openings, delivering the Halo to interior targets without breaching. The ring diameter can be reduced to 60cm for narrow apertures, though this increases the energy concentration and correspondingly the damage at impact. The 2.1-second charge cycle means the weapon is never used as a primary firearm; operators carry sidearms for immediate threats.
cultural_context: The KRE-1's prohibited status means it exists almost exclusively in military and paramilitary hands. Within military culture in GLMZ, the Halo carries a reputation as an executioner's weapon — precise, deliberate, theatrical. Stories of Halos used in high-profile political assassinations are a staple of conspiracy culture, and the violet ring has become a symbol in underground media representing state violence and corporate enforcement. Anti-corporate graffiti frequently depicts the glowing ring. Among soldiers who have used the weapon in combat, there is a marked tendency toward either pride or deep discomfort — it does not produce indifferent reactions.
known_users: High-tier mercenary companies with military contracts
story_hooks: A KRE-1 is used to assassinate a mid-district labor organizer — a target with no obvious military significance. The choice of weapon feels like a message. Someone wanted the death to look like official enforcement even if it wasn't.

A Tessera Corponation logistics manifest surfaces on the black market listing 40 KRE-1 units shipped to a destination that doesn't exist in any official registry. A fixer wants to know where those weapons actually went.

An operator who used the KRE-1 extensively during a corporate conflict is experiencing recurring nightmares of violet rings. A street-level psychtech thinks the superconducting coil's magnetic field may have caused subtle neural damage — and that Tessera knows.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist energy cannon with an oversized, dominating emitter head that tapers slightly from the breech. The weapon has the silhouette of a breach tool — industrial, purposeful, deliberately intimidating. The emitter head is a precisely engineered cylindrical assembly roughly the diameter of a coffee can, festooned with visible superconducting coil rings and heat dissipation fins. It reads as a weapon designed for institutional violence rather than personal combat.
physical_description.dimensions: 78cm overall length; 31cm width at the emitter head assembly; emitter bore approximately 12cm diameter; toroidal field projection 90cm diameter at standard calibration
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial and front-heavy — 8.4kg distributed toward the emitter head, requiring two-handed grip and shoulder bracing. Feels like shouldering industrial equipment rather than a conventional firearm.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite chassis with titanium alloy superconducting coil housing; anodized aluminum heat sink fins around the emitter head; internal tungsten shielding for electromagnetic containment
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray composite with brushed titanium accents; the emitter head shows polished aluminum fins with subtle oxidation patina suggesting field use; exposed superconducting coil rings beneath protective transparent sapphire plates
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray chassis with silver-white titanium emitter assembly; ice-blue indicator lights around the coil array; subtle violet luminescence visible only during charge cycle within the coil chamber
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer with textured side panels for two-handed purchase; integral accessory rail grip forward of the trigger guard; cool to the touch due to passive heat dissipation into the grip frame
distinctive_features: Visible superconducting coil rings arranged in a cylindrical array within the emitter head, visible through sapphire observation ports
Radial aluminum heat sink fins protruding from emitter assembly like a sci-fi cooling system
Dual charging indicator lights (blue) flanking the sight mount, brightening during 2.1-second charge cycle
Recessed muzzle opening with concentric ring geometry — designed to project the toroidal field
Integrated pressure relief vents along the barrel junction
Engraved power cell compartment on the underside marked with discharge counter (0-12)
Faint hairline fractures in the anodized finish from sustained electromagnetic stress during operation
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: TESSERA CORPONATION logo stamped in chrome on the left side of the chassis; KRE-1 'HALO' designation laser-etched on the emitter head; Tessera TC-20 power cell specification plate recessed into the grip; serial number on the underside compliance sticker (military registry)
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but visibly used — the aluminum fins show minor oxidation and stress marks; polymer chassis bears micro-abrasions from tactical handling and cover contact; sapphire observation ports are pristine (regularly maintained); internal superconducting coils show no visible damage but faint discoloration indicates thermal cycling
